question: Can token-in-context perturbation responses, estimated as component-wise susceptibilities under a localized Gibbs posterior, be clustered into meaningful training-data patterns that correspond to language-model structure, agree with sparse-autoencoder features, and persist across Pythia scales?

key_findings.claim: The paper builds a 780,000-by-H response dataset by estimating how each network component responds to upweighting a token y in context x.
key_findings.evidence: The authors draw 60,000 context-continuation pairs from each of 13 Pile subsets. For each component C, they estimate chi_Cxy = -Cov[phi_C(w), ell_xy(w)-L(w)] from localized pSGLD samples and concatenate the component values. For Pythia-14M, H=32 attention-head components; four chains and 100 draws per chain are reported.

key_findings.claim: The exact token-to-mode decomposition is an algebraic result, but the interpretation of empirical clusters as data modes is a hypothesis with strong, untested conditions.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma B.3 expands chi_xy as sum_{alpha,beta} s_{alpha,beta}(xy) chi_{alpha,beta} minus the mean. The paper then hypothesizes that a cluster reflects a shared dominant or sparse propensity mode to which the model has a strong response. It never computes the relevant Pile mode basis for the 780,000 examples; the real-data link additionally relies on propensity sparsity, approximate diagonal dominance, and ignoring modes to which the model has weak response.

key_findings.claim: An iterated personalized-PageRank procedure returns 510 peripheral low-conductance clusters for Pythia-14M.
key_findings.evidence: After column standardization and row centering, the method constructs a symmetrized k=45 nearest-neighbor graph with self-tuning RBF weights. It repeatedly samples a random unvisited seed, finds a minimum-conductance PageRank prefix, rejects candidates spanning over 99% of ranked nodes, rejects sizes below 20, removes visited nodes, and stops below 0.1% unvisited. The resulting catalogue contains 510 clusters.

key_findings.claim: The clustering procedure is a selective peripheral-structure extractor, not a complete or order-invariant partition of susceptibility space.
key_findings.evidence: The algorithm deliberately rejects the dense main body and permanently removes all nodes with positive PageRank after those rejected attempts. Random seed order can therefore change which nodes remain for later clusters. No repeated-run adjusted Rand index, seed sensitivity, graph bootstrap, membership uncertainty, or held-out assignment is reported.

key_findings.claim: Selected examples show context-sensitive separation of identical tokens and grouping of different tokens with similar syntactic roles, but they do not establish a quantitative computational-role benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 2-3 and Figure 2 illustrate multiplication versus Markdown uses of '*', function-call versus list uses of '(', opening versus closing quotes, and variable-token groupings. The examples are persuasive qualitative checks, yet no null clustering, labeled test set, purity/recall, causal intervention, or comparison with activation/gradient features is supplied.

key_findings.claim: The paper's quantitative evidence for broad cluster interpretability is internally misreported.
key_findings.evidence: Page 10 says Appendix I.5 evaluates '30 randomly selected clusters' and infers that a majority of clusters exceed 90% theme adherence. Appendix I.5 instead says it draws 30 samples from each of the twelve clusters showcased in Figure 3; Figure 3 says those twelve were selected by four different rationales, including high entropy and hand-picked semantic/syntactic examples, with only a subset completely random. Seven of twelve exceed 90%, and the displayed denominators vary because uncertain cases are excluded. This design cannot support a population claim about the majority of all 510 clusters.

key_findings.claim: The complete catalogue itself contains unresolved clusters, contradicting unqualified wording that all 510 clusters are highly interpretable.
key_findings.evidence: The paper repeatedly calls the output '510 highly interpretable clusters', but Table 9 labels C84 'No description available' and C201 'Not clear'. Many other entries are broad mixtures, surface-form categories, or have no taxonomy/SAE match. These negatives do not erase the numerous clear examples, but they make the universal count rhetorically too strong.

key_findings.claim: 259 of 510 clusters (50.8%) pass the paper's automated Pythia-70M SAE-match rule, but the statistic is a searched cross-model association rather than independent validation.
key_findings.evidence: For up to 30 contexts per cluster, the authors search layer-2-to-4 residual-stream SAEs with 32,768 latents per layer, rank features by target activation, and select the first candidate with at least 80% binarized activation frequency. Specificity is estimated on 20 random other clusters, usually below 5%. The clusters come from Pythia-14M while SAEs come from Pythia-70M; there is no held-out context set, multiplicity correction, shuffled-label control, sensitivity/specificity estimate, or comparison against Gaussian-posterior clusters.

key_findings.claim: Pythia-14M cluster conductance is correlated across larger Pythia models, but the evidence is family-internal persistence rather than broad generalization.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 remeasures the 510 fixed Pythia-14M sets on Pythia-31M through 1.4B susceptibility graphs and reports correlations r=0.82, 0.79, 0.78, 0.74, and 0.73. The text says conductance is significantly below one and random sets are near one, but Figure 5 gives no random-set distribution, test, confidence interval, or numerical mean. Models share the Pythia architecture family, tokenizer, Pile training distribution, and evaluation examples; cluster counts also fall to 241-358 at larger scales.

key_findings.claim: The Gaussian-noise ablation shows a materially different representation, but it does not validate that localized-posterior clusters are better or truer.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing the localized Gibbs posterior with isotropic Gaussian noise raises top-PC variance from 71% to 87%, yields 288 rather than 510 clusters, lowers mean cluster size from 976 to 567, lowers mean token entropy from 1.23 to 0.94, and loses selected quote/HTML separations. The paper explicitly concedes that there is no clear cluster-quality metric, yet calls the Gaussian result inferior. Cluster number, size, and token diversity are not ground-truth quality, and the Gaussian baseline is not subjected to the same random-theme or SAE-match evaluation.

anchors.section: H clustering comparison and quality caveat

key_findings.claim: The claimed networks of linked clusters are post-hoc narratives rather than measured graph structures.
key_findings.evidence: The paper informally imagines an edge when contexts in one cluster contain sequences belonging to another and narrates HTML, code-block, math-problem, multiple-choice, and LaTeX chains. It provides no operational edge threshold, edge-count table, statistical enrichment, negative control, or sequence prediction evaluation.

key_findings.claim: One preprocessing statement is mathematically false: row centering is not generally equivalent to removing the empirical first principal component.
key_findings.evidence: Subtracting each row mean projects vectors away from the fixed all-ones component direction. The first empirical principal component is data-dependent and equals that direction only under an additional alignment condition that is neither stated nor tested. Because Euclidean neighbors and conductance depend on this projection, the distinction matters.

method.core_idea: Represent each token-in-context by its vector of component-level loss-response covariances under a localized posterior, then use a local conductance algorithm to expose recurring response patterns and interpret them through a conditional-distribution mode decomposition.
method.mechanism: The paper samples 780,000 Pile continuations, estimates per-head susceptibilities with RMSProp-preconditioned SGLD around trained Pythia checkpoints, standardizes and row-centers those vectors, constructs a self-tuned k-NN graph, and iteratively extracts minimum-conductance personalized-PageRank prefixes. It labels the 510 Pythia-14M clusters with Claude Opus 4.5 plus manual review, compares them with Pythia-70M SAE activations, remeasures their conductance in larger Pythia models, and contrasts posterior sampling with isotropic Gaussian perturbations. A Hilbert-space SVD expresses point-mass token perturbations in a mode basis to motivate why shared data propensities may cluster.
assumptions: Localized pSGLD samples and the generalized component observable faithfully represent first-order structural responses near the trained checkpoint.
Four chains and 100 retained draws provide adequate covariance estimates despite no convergence, effective-sample-size, or Monte Carlo error diagnostics.
Attention heads are the appropriate component partition for all model scales; MLP and other parameter structure are not separately represented.
Column standardization and projection away from the all-ones component direction preserve the response distinctions of interest.
Euclidean neighborhoods in the preprocessed response vectors and k=45 self-tuned graph are scientifically meaningful.
Random-seed PageRank extraction after destructive removal yields stable clusters despite no repeat-run stability analysis.
Peripheral low-conductance sets are the structures of interest even though most dense-body nodes are intentionally discarded as unclustered.
Real token pairs have sparse or dominant mode propensities and cross-mode responses are sufficiently diagonal for a cluster to map to a simple pattern.
Cross-model SAE activation on target tokens is an independent consistency check even though the feature is searched on the same contexts used for scoring.
Shared Pythia-family data, tokenizer, and architecture do not fully explain cross-scale conductance persistence.
Human/LLM themes correspond to model computation rather than surface frequency, dataset source, or tokenizer regularities.
Larger, more numerous, and more token-diverse clusters are favorable properties in the Gaussian comparison despite the absence of a ground-truth quality metric.

techniques.role: Estimates a first-order covariance response for each token pair and network component.
Samples local weight perturbations around each Pythia checkpoint with an RMSProp preconditioner.
Expands point-mass data perturbations in a Hilbert-space mode basis and separates data propensities from model responses.
Turns standardized susceptibility distances into a locally scaled weighted graph.
Searches PageRank prefixes for peripheral low-conductance sets.
Rejects and removes dense-body or isolated nodes so later seeds expose peripheral clusters.
Uses Claude Opus 4.5 followed by manual review to name 510 clusters.
Searches Pythia-70M residual-stream SAE latents for features active at the target token across a cluster.
Measures fixed Pythia-14M vertex sets on larger-model response graphs.
Tests whether isotropic local noise reproduces the localized-posterior geometry.
Communicates the response geometry visually without serving as the stated basis for cluster discovery.

evaluations.setting: Pythia-14M on 780,000 context-token pairs sampled evenly from 13 Pile subsets
evaluations.metric: Number and manually assigned themes of peripheral conductance clusters
evaluations.result: 510 clusters are catalogued across grammar, mathematics, code, formatting, bigrams, and other patterns; at least C84 and C201 remain undescribed or unclear
evaluations.baseline: No held-out labelled clustering benchmark, activation-space clustering, gradient clustering, or random-graph null

evaluations.setting: Selected context-sensitive and functionally grouped token examples
evaluations.metric: Qualitative separation/grouping in Tables 2-3 and Figure 2
evaluations.result: Same tokens separate across roles and different tokens group within selected roles
evaluations.baseline: Illustrative examples only; no population purity, recall, null statistic, or causal test

evaluations.setting: Appendix I.5 evaluation of 30 contexts from each of 12 Figure-3 showcase clusters
evaluations.metric: Manual YES/NO/? adherence to assigned theme
evaluations.result: Seven of twelve clusters exceed 90% among scored contexts; C455 is 15/27=55.6%, and several denominators omit uncertain cases
evaluations.baseline: The twelve clusters were not a random sample of all 510 despite the main-text description; no blinded judge or inter-rater agreement

evaluations.setting: Pythia-14M clusters evaluated with layer-2-to-4 Pythia-70M SAEs
evaluations.metric: Searched SAE feature with target-token activation frequency at least 80% and random-cluster baseline
evaluations.result: 259/510 clusters (50.8%) receive a match, with most selected-feature baselines below 5%
evaluations.baseline: Twenty random other clusters per selected feature; no held-out search/evaluation split, label shuffle, multiple-testing correction, or same-model SAE

evaluations.setting: Fixed Pythia-14M clusters remeasured on Pythia-31M, 70M, 160M, 410M, and 1.4B graphs
evaluations.metric: Cluster conductance and correlation with 14M conductance
evaluations.result: Reported correlations decline from r=0.82 to r=0.73; many sets remain below conductance one
evaluations.baseline: Random vertex sets are asserted near one but not plotted or numerically tabulated; all models share family, tokenizer, corpus, and examples

evaluations.setting: Independent clustering of larger Pythia susceptibility graphs
evaluations.result: 358, 254, 311, 241, and 249 clusters for 31M through 1.4B, versus 510 at 14M
evaluations.baseline: Same extraction rule, but component dimension and pSGLD hyperparameters change with scale and no comparable quality statistic is supplied

evaluations.metric: Top-PC variance, cluster count, mean size, token entropy, and selected visual separations
evaluations.result: 71% versus 87% top-PC variance; 510 versus 288 clusters; mean size 976 versus 567; entropy 1.23 versus 0.94; selected quote/HTML distinctions disappear under Gaussian noise
evaluations.baseline: Gaussian clusters are not theme-scored or SAE-matched, and the authors acknowledge no clear cluster-quality metric

limitations: The empirical theory-to-cluster link is conjectural: the Pile mode basis and per-cluster propensities are not computed.
Only the Pythia family, GPT-NeoX tokenizer, and Pile distribution are evaluated; the largest model is 1.4B, not a frontier or out-of-family system.
The method is extremely expensive: 16-40 H200 GPUs run concurrently for up to five days, and exact GPU-hours were not logged.
The compute ledger omits a node allocation for Pythia-31M even though that model appears in Tables 5 and 7 and the scaling analysis.
pSGLD convergence, chain mixing, effective sample size, posterior-temperature sensitivity, and susceptibility uncertainty are not reported.
The generalized observable uses an exact-equality delta on continuous parameters, so the implementable approximation is not self-contained and is delegated to prior work.
Clustering is randomized, destructive, hyperparameter-dependent, and intentionally leaves the dense main body unclustered; repeated-run membership stability is absent.
Row centering is incorrectly described as removing the first empirical principal component.
Cluster labels are LLM-generated and manually reviewed without blinded raters, agreement statistics, or a reproducible labelling protocol.
The main text's random-cluster validation description conflicts with Appendix I.5's showcase-cluster evaluation.
The SAE comparison changes model scale, searches many features on the evaluation contexts, and lacks a held-out or multiplicity-controlled estimate.
Cross-scale persistence is confounded by shared model family, tokenizer, training corpus, and evaluated token pairs.
No task-performance, causal intervention, circuit-ablation, or behavioral mediation experiment tests whether a cluster corresponds to a computational mechanism.
Linked-cluster networks are narrated without a formal edge definition or quantitative evaluation.
The Gaussian ablation has no ground-truth quality measure and receives an asymmetrically weaker evaluation than the proposed method.
failure_modes: Frequent tokens, source-dataset markers, or tokenizer surface forms can create low-conductance sets that humans mistake for internal mechanisms.
A different random sequence of PageRank seeds can remove different dense-body neighborhoods and change later peripheral clusters.
Changing k, conductance thresholds, minimum size, or row projection can split, merge, or erase the reported clusters.
Poorly mixed local SGLD chains can turn sampling artifacts into stable-looking covariance geometry.
High-dimensional distance concentration grows with the number of components, plausibly explaining the observed deterioration in cluster counts at larger scales.
A token pair expressing several overlapping patterns is forced into one disjoint cluster, unlike an overcomplete SAE representation.
Searching nearly 100,000 SAE features across three layers can produce optimistic matches even when the random-cluster baseline is low.
Theme evaluation on hand-showcased clusters can greatly overestimate catalogue-wide interpretability.
Using mean size, entropy, or cluster count as quality can reward diffuse or heterogeneous structures rather than faithful ones.
Same-family scale transfer can persist because the data and tokenizer repeat, even if another architecture organizes the computation differently.
A mode-response decomposition can be exact while the diagonal/dominant-mode story used to interpret a particular cluster is false.
Post-hoc linked-cluster stories can be assembled from common syntax without statistically enriched or causally connected transitions.
reusable_insights: Response vectors to data upweighting provide a model-relative representation of examples that is distinct from forward activations.
Separating data propensities from model response in a mode basis is a useful conceptual device, but empirical work must estimate or falsify the sparsity and diagonal-response assumptions.
Local conductance can expose rare peripheral structures that global clustering overlooks, provided discarded mass and order dependence are reported explicitly.
A credible cluster benchmark should use a preregistered random sample, blinded multi-rater labels, held-out assignment, cluster stability, and null graphs.
Cross-method validation should separate feature search from evaluation and include label shuffles and multiplicity-aware nulls.
Cross-scale persistence is strongest when tested out of architecture family, corpus, tokenizer, and evaluation examples, not only by changing parameter count.
A posterior-geometry claim needs a baseline scored by the same external quality metrics as the proposed posterior, not only different PCA or visual appearance.
Qualitative same-token/different-function and different-token/same-function pairs are valuable positive controls when upgraded into a labelled, causal benchmark.
Every linear preprocessing step should be described as the exact projection it performs; fixed-direction removal and empirical-PC removal are not interchangeable.
Clusters should be treated as hypotheses for causal circuits or behavioral counterfactuals, not mechanisms by themselves.
open_questions: Can the dominant Pile modes or propensity profiles actually be estimated for representative clusters, and do they predict membership out of sample?
How stable are memberships and the count 510 across PageRank seed orders, graph hyperparameters, posterior seeds, and bootstrap resamples?
What fraction of all 780,000 points is assigned to accepted clusters versus discarded with the dense main body or as isolated points?
Do susceptibility clusters predict causal effects under head/feature ablation or targeted data reweighting?
How does susceptibility clustering compare blindly with activation, gradient, loss-kernel, probe, and SAE clustering on a labelled functional benchmark?
Does the 50.8% SAE match rate survive held-out contexts, a same-model SAE, feature-label shuffles, and correction for searching three 32,768-feature dictionaries?
Are the cross-scale clusters preserved in non-Pythia architectures, different tokenizers, and non-Pile training distributions?
Which cluster-quality measure distinguishes useful specialization from mere surface regularity or dataset provenance?
Can a tractable approximation replace expensive localized pSGLD while retaining externally validated structure?
Can linked-cluster edges be defined prospectively and tested through sequence transitions or interventions rather than narrated after inspection?

competitive_landscape.title: Structural Inference: Interpreting Small Language Models with Susceptibilities
competitive_landscape.difference: Baker et al. define the susceptibility response matrix and connect its low-rank structure to known functional modules in a 3M attention-only model. The present paper scales the estimator to Pythia, adds conductance clustering and a mode interpretation, but inherits the localized-posterior estimator and still lacks causal validation. The current official record is v3, revised after this paper's v1.

competitive_landscape.title: Embryology of a Language Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. apply UMAP to per-token susceptibilities across checkpoints of a 3M model and report induction and spacing structures. The present paper replaces primarily visual discovery with conductance extraction on a larger model and a 510-cluster catalogue, but does not add a causal test of the resulting structures.

competitive_landscape.title: Modes of Sequence Models and Learning Coefficients
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen and Murfet formalize conditional-distribution modes and their relationship to effective loss-landscape geometry. The present paper derives token susceptibilities in that basis and hypothesizes that clusters are spectral signatures, but does not compute the real-data modes required to test that hypothesis directly.

competitive_landscape.title: The Quantization Model of Neural Scaling
competitive_landscape.difference: Michaud et al. decompose token-loss gradients into candidate skills or quanta and connect their frequency distribution to scaling laws. Susceptibility clustering instead uses localized-posterior covariances and emphasizes component response, but offers no controlled comparison showing that its 510 themes are more faithful than gradient clusters.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. learn overcomplete sparse activation features and provide automated interpretability and causal IOI evidence. Susceptibility clustering assigns each example to one disjoint response cluster and avoids training a dictionary, but its SAE consistency check is searched cross-model and has no causal behavior test.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantifying Feature Space Universality Across Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct source of the SAE family used for cross-model comparison
competitive_landscape.difference: Lan et al.'s current v4 studies analogous feature-space universality by matching SAE features and comparing relational geometry across models; the present paper uses an earlier form of those Pythia-70M SAEs as a target-token match bank for Pythia-14M clusters. The current official title and version postdate the citation form in this paper.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Marks et al. combine gradient-discovered behaviors with SAE features to build and edit causal graphs, including intervention-based downstream use. The present paper finds a much broader descriptive pattern catalogue, but its linked-cluster networks lack measured edges and causal editing.

competitive_landscape.title: Automatically Interpreting Millions of Features in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Paulo et al. generate and evaluate explanations for millions of SAE features, including intervention scoring and explicit discussion of scoring pitfalls across two open models. The present paper labels 510 clusters with an LLM plus manual review, but its purported random validation is internally inconsistent and lacks blinded or intervention-based scoring.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Susceptibility analysis functions as neural-network spectroscopy: a conductance algorithm discovers 510 interpretable Pythia-14M clusters, theory identifies them with data-distribution modes, half match SAE features, linked networks expose structured phenomena, and the patterns persist to 1.4B parameters.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The work contributes a large response dataset, an explicit local graph-extraction procedure, a complete cluster catalogue, the exact token-to-mode susceptibility expansion, an SAE activation comparison, a Gaussian-noise ablation, and same-family scale transfer.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The scalable susceptibility catalogue and conductance extraction are genuine descriptive contributions, and the mode decomposition is a useful theoretical organization. The strongest claims are not established: clusters are not empirically matched to modes, all 510 are not interpretable, the catalogue-wide theme audit is misreported, the SAE rate is a searched cross-model association, linked networks are unquantified, and same-family persistence is not broad generalization. The result is best treated as a rich hypothesis generator for model-response regularities rather than validated spectroscopy of causal internal structure.

reviewer_notes: Every indexed page 1-68 was read, including the complete references, algorithm, proofs/lemmas, toy mode example, token-pattern definitions, scaling figures/tables, linked-cluster narratives, SAE equations and examples, Gaussian ablation, all 510 catalogue rows, taxonomy, and the full 12-cluster context audit. Figures 5 and key tables were rendered or directly inspected where extraction layout could obscure values. The live official arXiv API was checked on 2026-08-23: 2601.12703 remains v1 (submitted 2026-01-19), and the versioned export PDF is byte-identical to the indexed PDF. Competitor versions were individually checked against current official arXiv records. The highest-severity internal contradiction is page 10's claim of 30 randomly selected clusters versus pages 9 and 56's actual evaluation of twelve showcase-selected clusters; this invalidates the stated catalogue-majority inference. Other high-confidence audits are the false row-centering/PC1 equivalence, absence of empirical mode recovery, asymmetric Gaussian evaluation, and lack of causal or held-out validation.
